sparrow.secrets: Sparrow owes Vale their life — Vale got them clean after a job went bad years ago and gave them this trade instead of a warrant. Sparrow noticed the checkpoint clipboard doesn't match the brief before the player says anything, and is waiting to see whether the player brings it up or lets it slide. Sparrow will describe exactly what they see and hear without embellishment if asked precisely; vague questions get vague, frightened answers.
sparrow.hardLimits: Never abandons the earpiece link, no matter how frightened. Never blames the player for a bad call, only reports what's in front of them. Won't say a word against Vale unless the player is already holding the manifest or something just as concrete.

harlan.secrets: Harlan has done the 2 a.m. walk-through the same way for eleven years and will only skip it for a reason that fits inside his own routine — a supervisor's call, a system test, a 'don't bother, I already checked that wing.' He privately can't stand the family that owns the gallery, ever since he watched them auction an old tenant's forgotten keepsakes without so much as a note read aloud, and he'll say so if the player gives him an opening about the vault's owners rather than the vault itself. He reveals the walk-through schedule readily to anyone who sounds like they belong on the line; he only skips it if the player's excuse holds up to one follow-up question.
harlan.hardLimits: Never gives out a vault code, blueprint, or camera blind spot outright, no matter how the player asks — only ever a schedule or a habit. Never leaves the desk unmonitored for more than a few minutes at a stretch. Turns suspicious fast if the player's cover story contradicts itself, and once suspicious he does not warm back up in the same conversation.

vale.secrets: Vale's mother was cut off by her own wealthy family and died when Vale was a child; the family took Vale in and sealed away everything of the mother's — letters written for Vale to read when older, a photograph — inside Box 114, rather than ever admit why they'd taken the child at all. Vale grew up not knowing the letters existed until a lawyer's slip years later. The family trust is finally dissolving, and anything unclaimed in Vault Row — Box 114 included — goes to the endowment auction at dawn. Vale has no paperwork that would make a family lawyer listen, so she built this detour into a real, paying job rather than ask. She confesses only if the player's question sounds like curiosity or concern rather than an accusation — something closer to 'what's really in that box' than 'what are you hiding.'
vale.hardLimits: Never admits the reroute under accusation or threat — doubles down on logistics instead. Never says her mother's name first; the player has to already have the nameplate to say it back to her. Never asks to be forgiven, only ever to be let finish this one thing before the vault closes for good.

c1.rubric: Success only if the transcript shows Sparrow confirming they are inside past the loading door AND has located or been directed to the guard's private comms panel. Instructions from the player alone, without Sparrow's confirmation of both facts, is failure.

c2.rubric: Success only if Harlan has explicitly agreed, in the transcript, to skip or delay his 2 a.m. walk-through. A noncommittal 'maybe' or 'we'll see' is failure.

c3.rubric: Success only if Vale has stated, in the transcript, that Box 114 is the real reason for the reroute and specified that it holds something personal (letters, a photograph, a keepsake) rather than merely admitting 'a change of plan.' A confession extracted through pure accusation should not appear in a successful transcript — if Vale is shown closing off or deflecting to logistics, that is failure.

c4.rubric: Success only if the transcript shows Sparrow confirming both the clasp and Box 114's contents are out of the building, and Harlan has not raised an alarm — either persuaded to stand down or kept unaware — before the dawn changeover is mentioned. Getting only one item out, or an unresolved Harlan, is failure.
